inputs.text: These health workers in Nigeria are escalating tensions by launching disruptive protests instead of accepting reforms that would strengthen national authority and bring accountability to the sector. On Thursday, the Joint Health Sector Unions and the Assembly of Healthcare Professional Associations took to the streets in Abuja, gathering at the Unity Fountain in Maitama to oppose reform bills before the National Assembly. This kind of public agitation undermines social order, reveals a rejection of personal responsibility, and prioritizes union interests over the stability that families depend on for essential services. It's yet another case of self-serving groups chipping away at the traditions and authority that hold a nation together.
